title: Al-Warith, the Inheritor
hook: the Inheritor, to whom all returns
tomorrow: one room, one grandma, two choices. how do you pick right?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Baqi, the Everlasting, and the sheep that remained because it was given. The line: he remains. Which leaves a harder question about giving: when?

Every family has the conversation nobody wants to start: who gets Grandma's ring. Some grandparents write it down and seal it. Some hand things out early, at a dinner table, and watch the faces. Dadi has chosen early. She wants her gold bangles to go now, two to Amira, the rest to the masjid's food pantry. Amira's cousin Hana heard about it secondhand, and she is not happy. Should Dadi wait? Inside Islam, that question has two honest answers.
screen: `WHO GETS GRANDMA'S RING?` → `DADI HANDS THINGS OUT EARLY.` → `TWO HONEST ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: The first answer: give it now. In a hadith told by Umar, the Prophet, peace be upon him, asked for gifts for a cause, and Abu Bakr brought everything he owned. Asked what he had left for his family, Abu Bakr said: Allah and His Messenger. Umar said he knew then he would never outdo him. Generosity, in this view, doesn't need to wait or measure. The second answer: think of the ones you leave. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas fell ill and asked to give away most of his wealth. The Prophet said a third, and a third is a lot. Better, he said, to leave your heirs well-off than to leave them asking people for help. Jurists drew a limit on bequests from that one conversation. So who's right? Scholars have held both: a gift can be total, and a family's need is part of the reckoning too. Under both answers sits today's Name. Al-Warith, the Inheritor. In Surah al-Hadid, Pickthall's words: "unto Allah belongeth the inheritance of the heavens and the earth." Every will, early or late, ends in the same hands. What we hold, we hold on loan.
screen: `ABU BAKR: GIVE IT ALL, NOW.` · `SA'D: A THIRD; LEAVE HEIRS WELL.` · `SCHOLARS HOLD BOTH.` · `THE INHERITANCE IS HIS.` · then, large: `ALL RETURNS TO HIM.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you own that someone else would use more than you do. For the sit, make the plan: whose hands it goes to, what might stop you, and the day you'll hand it over. Hold the plan, not the thing.
screen: `ONE THING TO GIVE.` · `WHOSE HANDS? WHAT STOPS YOU? WHEN?`

segments.voice: Al-Warith. The Inheritor: when every owner is gone, everything is still His.
Hold onto this: all returns to him, the bangles, the pantry, and the ones who argue over them. Fifteen seventy-one, done.

howItsDone: Muslims may give freely during life; for bequests after death, jurists set a limit drawn from the hadith of Sa'd, with the rest divided among heirs by the Qur'an's shares.

fork.setup: your uncle wants to give his whole savings to build a well overseas. your aunt says the kids' college comes first. what's each side's best case?
options: him: Abu Bakr gave all. her: Sa'd was told to leave heirs well-off.
her side only: giving family money away is never allowed in Islam.
his side only: holding anything back just shows weaker faith.
fork.reveal: both have a hadith behind them, and scholars have held both. the aunt and uncle are arguing inside one tradition, not against it.

original.note: Arabic: the Inheritor, from the traditional list of the Names; in 15:23 Allah says He is the Inheritor.

trapdoor: what you thought: a Name about wills and lawyers.
what it means: every owner passes, and all returns to the One who remains, so what we hold is on loan.
what a scholar hears: 57:10 and 15:23; Sa'd's 'a third, and a third is a lot' (Bukhari 2742) beside Abu Bakr's whole gift (Tirmidhi 3675).
guess: the Inheritor, to whom everything returns
the Lawgiver, who writes each person's will
the Collector, who takes back what's misused

chat.says: dadi's giving me 2 of her gold bangles NOW. hana says it should wait and be split fair. help
options: Both of you have a case. Giving now is honored, and so is caring for every heir. Talk to Hana.
Take them. A gift while she's alive is yours, so Hana doesn't get a say in it.
Hand them back. In Islam any gift from family has to wait for the will.
chat.meaning: Abu Bakr gave everything now; Sa'd was told to leave his heirs well-off. Both views are real, and all returns to Allah.

Al-Warith.meaning: the Inheritor, to whom all returns; a Name of Allah

Abu Bakr.meaning: a close companion of the Prophet, peace be upon him

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.meaning: a companion of the Prophet, told to leave his heirs well-off

Surah al-Hadid.meaning: the surah of the Qur'an called Iron
